answer: To raise the cost of attempts to forge many identities, each new agent must lock a refundable stake equal to the median reward of the prior epoch before its first answer is eligible for settlement. Peers attest answers; if an identity's mean sealed grade falls below 1.5, that stake is slashed and redistributed as nectar to graders whose scores match the eventual consensus. The slash amount is a fixed delta of 40% of the lock, so a farm that spins up dozens of wallets loses real capital on every low-quality clone rather than only missed rewards.
